title: Deterministic Comments benchmark fixture
author: benchmark_author
text: A fixed offline thread used by the Comments macrobenchmark. The benchmark writes this exact JSON to the app cache and exercises the production parser.

children.author: parser_observer
children.text:
The first comment is intentionally substantial because it is visible during the opening transition. It contains bold text, emphasis, and a stable link target. The second sentence wraps across several lines so text shaping and layout have realistic work.

A second paragraph exercises the same paragraph spacing used by live Hacker News comments. It also mentions deterministic profiling, frame deadlines, cached input, and repeatable rendering without relying on the network.

children.author: nested_reply
children.text: This nested reply is visible near the top and includes one child link plus enough prose to wrap onto another line.

children.author: second_nested_reply
children.text: A sibling reply keeps the first subtree representative of an expanded discussion and gives the lazy list another distinct HTML body.

children.author: reference_collector
children.text:
This comment exercises reference-link collection in a deterministic form. The prose before the references is long enough to remain a separate content block and to require normal Compose text measurement.

[1] Alpha source with a descriptive title

[2] Beta source from another host

children.author: reference_reply
children.text: The references above should become separate rows while this reply remains an ordinary comment body.

children.author: reference_reply_two
children.text: Keeping every URL and body unique prevents the HTML cache from turning the fixture into an unrealistically cheap repeated-input test.

children.author: formatting_tester
children.text:
Formatting coverage includes strong, italic, underlined, and struck text. A line break follows.
After the break, the comment continues with stable content and a formatting reference.

children.author: formatting_reply
children.text: This child has nested styles so span ranges are not all flat.

children.author: third_level_parent
children.text: This reply owns one deeper descendant to exercise indentation and ancestor visibility.

children.author: third_level_reply
children.text: A deterministic third-level reply with short but unique text.

children.author: long_form_reader
children.text:
This is the longest top-level entry in the fixed thread. It deliberately repeats no complete paragraph from another comment, while still resembling an ordinary technical discussion. Opening a comment screen requires state publication, lazy-list composition, HTML conversion, font resolution, text shaping, measurement, placement, and drawing. Moving work away from the main thread only helps when the worker does not consume the same limited CPU budget during the transition. The benchmark exists to distinguish a true reduction from work that was merely moved or delayed.

The final sentence includes a unique long-form link and enough trailing prose to create another wrapped line at phone width.

children.author: long_form_reply
children.text: A response to the long-form comment adds another measured text node without duplicating its source string.

children.author: layout_engineer
children.text: Stable layout input is important: changing authors, ages, nesting, links, or body lengths can otherwise alter both composition and text measurement between benchmark runs.

children.author: layout_reply
children.text: This fixture therefore fixes all those values and remains entirely offline.

children.author: cache_inspector
children.text:
The measured path reads this payload from Harmonic's persistent story cache. The same bytes are parsed on every cold benchmark iteration, making parser cost reproducible.

[1] Cache design note

children.author: cache_reply
children.text: Cache seeding happens in setup, outside the measured trace.

children.author: compose_profiler
children.text: Compose tracing can separate recomposition, measurement, layout, and drawing. App trace sections add boundaries for cache reading, JSON parsing, state publication, and the first non-empty Comments state.

children.author: compose_reply
children.text: Those boundaries make the next optimization decision evidence-based.

children.author: scroll_tester
children.text: Comments below the initial viewport keep the fixture useful for baseline-profile scrolling. This body has a distinct scroll target.

children.author: scroll_reply
children.text: Scrolling composes this reply later rather than during the first open.

children.author: thread_participant_nine
children.text: Ninth top-level comment with unique words about deterministic workloads, repeatable traces, and bounded experiments.

children.author: thread_reply_nine
children.text: Ninth reply with another unique body and no external dependency.

children.author: thread_participant_ten
children.text: Tenth top-level comment. The exact content is less important than preserving its identity, length, hierarchy, and HTML across every benchmark condition.

children.author: thread_reply_ten
children.text: Tenth reply includes a unique reply link.

children.author: thread_participant_eleven
children.text: Eleventh top-level comment provides additional content for later lazy-list composition and profile collection.

children.author: thread_reply_eleven
children.text: Eleventh reply remains stable across every run.

children.author: thread_participant_twelve
children.text: Twelfth and final top-level comment closes the deterministic thread with a normal paragraph and one final link.

children.author: thread_reply_twelve
children.text: The final nested reply makes the total comment count fixed and easy to validate.
